hook.situation: You see clues, but you are not fully sure yet: the sky is getting dark, a friend is not replying, or a bus may be late.
objectives: Use A/V-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 for a soft prediction or impression.
Use V/A-나 봐요 and -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 when a visible clue supports the guess.
Use V/A-(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 when something is possible and the listener should be ready for it.
hook.whyItMatters: English learners often say 'I think' for everything. Korean gives you different levels of certainty: a soft guess, an evidence-based inference, and an open possibility. Choosing the right one keeps you from sounding too sure or too vague.

grammarNotes.title: A/V-(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 - I think it will / it seems
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 것 같아요 puts a soft layer around your guess. You are saying, 'It seems that way to me,' not claiming it as a fact.
grammarNotes.formation: For a future or uncertain guess, attach -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요: 오다 becomes 올 것 같아요, 늦다 becomes 늦을 것 같아요, 맛있다 becomes 맛있을 것 같아요. For a current verb guess, use -는 것 같아요: 비가 오는 것 같아요. For a current adjective guess, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요: 바쁜 것 같아요, 좋은 것 같아요. For a past guess, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 or -았/었던 것 같아요 depending on the predicate.

examples.ko: 하늘이 흐려서 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: haneuri heuryeoseo biga ol geot gatayo.
examples.en: The sky is cloudy, so I think it will rain.
examples.note: Visible clue plus soft future prediction.

examples.ko: 길이 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: giri makyeoseo jogeum neujeul geot gatayo.
examples.en: Traffic is heavy, so I think I will be a little late.
examples.note: A polite warning before being late.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 사람이 많아서 맛있을 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: i kapeneun sarami manaseo masisseul geot gatayo.
examples.en: This cafe has many people, so I think it will be good.
examples.note: You are guessing from popularity, not reporting a fact.

examples.en: It seems my friend is still on the way.
examples.note: Use -는 것 같아요 for a current action.

contrastPairs.explanation: 것 같아요 is softer and less certain. -ㄹ 거예요 sounds more like a confident prediction.

a.en: It looks like it will rain.

contrastPairs.explanation: -ㄹ 것 같아요 looks forward. -는 것 같아요 guesses about an action happening now.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not translate 'I think' word for word with 생각하다 in quick predictions. Korean often uses 것 같아요.

exceptions: When you know the fact, do not soften it: 지금 비가 와요 is better than 지금 비가 오는 것 같아요 if you are literally seeing rain.
Adjectives use modifier forms: 바쁜 것 같아요, 좋은 것 같아요, 피곤한 것 같아요.
같아요 here is part of a grammar frame; do not explain it only as 같다 meaning 'same.'

grammarNotes.title: V/A-나 봐요 / -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 - it seems from evidence
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 나 봐요 means your guess is not random. Something you saw, heard, or noticed is pushing you toward that conclusion.
grammarNotes.formation: Verbs and 있다/없다 usually take -나 봐요: 오나 봐요, 있나 봐요, 없나 봐요. Descriptive adjectives take -(으)ㄴ가 봐요: 바쁜가 봐요, 좋은가 봐요, 피곤한가 봐요. Nouns take 인가 봐요: 휴일인가 봐요, 학생인가 봐요.

examples.ko: 사람들이 우산을 꺼내네요. 비가 오나 봐요.
examples.romanization: saramdeuri usaneul kkeonaeneyo. biga ona bwayo.
examples.en: People are taking out umbrellas. I guess it is raining.
There is no reply. I guess they are really busy.

examples.ko: 불이 꺼져 있어요. 오늘 쉬는 날인가 봐요.
examples.romanization: buri kkeojyeo isseoyo. oneul swineun naringa bwayo.
examples.en: The lights are off. I guess today is a day off.
Their voice is quiet. I guess they are tired.
examples.note: A careful inference from how someone sounds.

contrastPairs.explanation: 것 같아요 is a broad impression or prediction. 나 봐요 stresses a clue you noticed.

b.en: I guess my friend is tired.

contrastPairs.explanation: Use direct statements for your own clear feelings. Use -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 when you infer someone else's state.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: Do not use evidence-based inference for your own obvious feeling unless you intentionally sound self-observing or joking.

exceptions: 있다 and 없다 pattern like verbs: 있나 봐요, 없나 봐요.
In casual speech, the ending can shorten to -나 봐 or -(으)ㄴ가 봐.
If you have no clue, use 아마 or -ㄹ지도 몰라요 instead of -나 봐요.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 - might / may
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -ㄹ지도 몰라요 keeps a possibility open. It often functions like a gentle warning: this may happen, so prepare for it.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -ㄹ지도 몰라요 after vowel stems and -을지도 몰라요 after consonant stems: 오다 becomes 올지도 몰라요, 늦다 becomes 늦을지도 몰라요, 많다 becomes 많을지도 몰라요. For past possibility, use -았/었을지도 몰라요: 벌써 갔을지도 몰라요.

examples.en: It might rain. Take an umbrella.
examples.note: The possibility leads to practical advice.
You are not sure, but it is possible.

examples.en: My friend might have already left.

contrastPairs.explanation: 것 같아요 usually feels like a stronger impression. -ㄹ지도 몰라요 leaves the chance open.

a.en: I think I will be late.

contrastPairs.explanation: Use -ㄹ 것 같아요 when you lean toward that outcome. Use -ㄹ지도 몰라요 when you want to warn about a possibility.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: This is a fixed pattern. Keep -ㄹ지도 before 몰라요.

exceptions: In casual speech, 몰라요 can become 몰라: 늦을지도 몰라.
The pattern means 'might,' not simply 'do not know.'
For a strong denial, later chapters use -ㄹ 리가 없어요, the opposite of this open possibility.

exampleSentence.en: I will probably be a little late.
exampleSentence.note: 아마 naturally reinforces a soft guess.
A common clue before a weather guess.

extendedVocabulary.english: to be cloudy; to be blurry

exampleSentence.ko: 하늘이 흐려서 비가 올 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: The sky is cloudy, so I think it will rain.

exampleSentence.note: 비 takes 이/가 and pairs with 오다.
A visible clue for 비가 오나 봐요.

exampleSentence.ko: 길이 막혀서 조금 늦을 것 같아요.
exampleSentence.en: Traffic is heavy, so I think I will be a little late.
There is no reply. I guess they are busy.
Their voice is quiet. I guess they are tired.
exampleSentence.note: Use for inferred tiredness in someone else.

exampleSentence.en: Since we are not sure, let's check.
exampleSentence.note: Useful when deciding how strong your guess is.

exampleSentence.en: There is a chance it will rain.
exampleSentence.note: A noun-based way to talk about probability.

exampleSentence.en: We can infer from the clue.
exampleSentence.note: Names the thinking process behind the grammar.
In -ㄹ지도 몰라요, 모르다 is part of a fixed possibility pattern.

exampleSentence.en: I think it will rain soon.

exampleSentence.note: Often used for a short wait or quick change.

extendedDialogue.setting: Two friends look at weather and message clues before meeting someone.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 하늘이 갑자기 흐려졌어요. 곧 비가 올 것 같아요.
lines.romanization: haneuri gapjagi heuryeojyeosseoyo. got biga ol geot gatayo.
lines.en: The sky suddenly got cloudy. I think it will rain soon.
lines.grammarNote: A visible clue supports a soft prediction.

lines.speaker: 지훈

lines.romanization: saramdeuri usaneul kkeonaeneyo. beolsseo biga jogeum ona bwayo.

lines.speaker: 민서

lines.romanization: sujin ssi dapjangdo eopseoyo. mani bappeunga bwayo.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: If the bus is stuck too, she might be a little late.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: Since we are not sure, let's wait inside the cafe.

readingText.title: Reading clues before a meeting
readingText.body: 민서는 약속 장소로 가는 길에 하늘이 갑자기 흐려지는 것을 봤어요. 그래서 곧 비가 올 것 같다고 생각했어요. 지하철역 앞에서는 사람들이 우산을 꺼내고 있었어요. 민서는 비가 조금 오나 봐요라고 말했어요. 그런데 친구 수진 씨는 아직 답장이 없었어요. 지훈은 수진 씨가 바쁜가 봐요, 조금 늦을지도 몰라요라고 했어요. 두 사람은 확실하지 않으니까 밖에서 기다리지 않고 카페 안으로 들어갔어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Minseo saw the sky suddenly getting cloudy on the way to the meeting place, so she thought it would rain soon. In front of the subway station, people were taking out umbrellas, so she inferred that it was raining. Their friend Su-jin had not replied yet, so Jihoon guessed she might be busy and a little late. Since they were not sure, they waited inside a cafe instead of outside.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 민서는 무엇을 보고 비가 올 것 같다고 생각했어요?
사람들이 우산을 꺼내는 것은 어떤 단서예요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 비가 조금 오나 봐요라고 추측할 수 있는 단서예요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 두 사람은 왜 카페 안으로 들어갔어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 확실하지 않았고 밖에서 기다리기 불편해서 카페 안으로 들어갔어요.

culturalNote.title: Soft guesses in Korean conversation
culturalNote.body: Korean speakers often soften guesses with 것 같아요, 나 봐요, or -ㄹ지도 몰라요, especially when talking about another person's situation. It sounds more careful than declaring a reason you cannot fully know.
culturalNote.tip: Use direct Korean when you know the fact, but use these forms when you are reading clues: 답장이 없네요. 바쁜가 봐요.

inlineExercises.prompt: You see dark clouds and want a soft prediction. Which sentence fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: -ㄹ 것 같아요 makes a soft prediction from the clue.

inlineExercises.prompt: People are taking out umbrellas. Which form best shows inference from evidence?
inlineExercises.explanation: -나 봐요 says your guess comes from a clue you noticed.

inlineExercises.prompt: You are not sure, but the bus may be late. Which sentence fits?
Complete: 답장이 없네요. 많이 바쁜___ 봐요.
Fix the sentence: 비가 올 모르다.
inlineExercises.explanation: The possibility pattern keeps -ㄹ지도 before 몰라요.

bullets: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 gives a soft prediction or impression: 비가 올 것 같아요.
-나 봐요 / -(으)ㄴ가 봐요 means the guess comes from a clue: 우산을 꺼내네요. 비가 오나 봐요.
-(으)ㄹ지도 몰라요 keeps a possibility open: 버스가 늦을지도 몰라요.
Do not use evidence-based inference for your own obvious feeling. Say 피곤해요, not 저는 피곤한가 봐요.
summaryCard.nextChapterTeaser: Next, you will explain reasons more naturally when a plan changes because something happened.
